core_conclusion: The declared unguided finite-contact model is anchored to the published 2H MoSSe GSFE, whose lateral registry landscape contains a non-removable inversion-odd component.

panels.question: Is the 2H registry-space inversion asymmetry removable by translation, and how does it compare with 3R controls?
processing_notes: Exact-zero symmetric control is displayed at a 1e-18 plotting floor and labeled 0.
A_min and chi1 are direct diagnostics from the same audit.

caption: Figure 1. Credible model input and registry-space inversion asymmetry. (a) Schematic of the unguided finite contact: the center of mass is free in the full two-dimensional registry plane, loading is applied along the declared ±y crystallographic axis, and the prepared state is the lowest-energy zero-force stable minimum. This schematic is illustrative and is not numerical evidence. (b) Published three-shell 2H MoSSe generalized stacking-fault-energy landscape used as the conservative input, shown in lattice coordinates. (c) Translation-minimized odd-RMS fraction for the 2H landscape and 3R controls; the exact-zero symmetric control is placed at 10^-18 only as a plotting floor and is labeled 0. The displayed A_min and chi1 quantify the same coordinate-independent asymmetry audit. Lateral registry inversion asymmetry is not identified with physical Janus-polarity reversal.
